title: Kth Largest Element In An Array
statement: Given an array of integers and a number k, return the kth largest value. This is the kth in sorted order from biggest to smallest, so repeated values count separately. Try to do better than sorting the whole array.

example.caption: k = 2. Sorted from biggest: 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. The 2nd largest is 5.

idea.sentence: Keep the k biggest numbers in a min-heap, and its top, the smallest of them, is the kth largest.

jargon.plain: A container where the smallest item is always on top. Push and pop cost about log of its size.
Quicksort that only follows the side holding the answer. It partitions around a pivot, then ignores the other side.
Rearrange a range around a pivot value so smaller values are on its left and the rest on its right. The pivot ends in its final sorted place.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the array and k, e.g. [3,2,1,5,6,4], 2

compare.optimalLabel: Quickselect, average case (the heap is n log k)

rows.name: Sort the array
rows.note: Simple and often good enough. Sort numerically, not as strings.

rows.name: Min-heap of size k
rows.note: One push and at most one pop per number on a heap of at most k + 1 items.

rows.name: Quickselect
rows.note: Partition and follow one side only. The worst case needs consistently bad pivots or many equal values.

fast.takeaway: You do not need the whole order, only the border at position k. The heap tracks that border, and quickselect finds it directly.

stages.title: Start a heap
stages.note: Create an empty min-heap. It will only ever hold the k biggest numbers seen so far.

stages.title: Push
stages.note: Push each number into the min-heap.

stages.title: Trim to k
stages.note: If the heap holds more than k numbers, pop the smallest. It cannot be the kth largest.

stages.title: Read the top
stages.note: After the last number the heap holds the k biggest. Its top is the kth largest.

stages.title: Find the target index
stages.note: In ascending order the kth largest sits at index n - k. That is the spot to hit.

stages.title: Partition
stages.note: Pick a pivot and rearrange the live range around it. The pivot lands in its final sorted place.

stages.title: Follow one side
stages.note: If the pivot is left of the target, keep the right part. If right of it, keep the left part.

stages.title: Done
stages.note: When the pivot lands exactly on the target index, that value is the answer.

edges.title: One element
edges.why: The heap holds one number and the top is the answer. Quickselect has target index 0 and stops at once.

edges.title: k equals n
edges.why: The kth largest is the minimum. Nothing is ever popped from the heap.

edges.title: Duplicates count
edges.why: Each 2 is its own entry in the ranking. Do not de-duplicate first.

edges.title: Mixed digits
edges.why: Numeric order, not string order. As strings, 9 would beat 100.

gotchas.text: nums.sort() without a comparator sorts as strings: [10, 9, 100] becomes [10, 100, 9]. Use nums.sort((a, b) => b - a). There is no built-in heap, so the shown file has a small one.
Quickselect reorders the array. Copy it first if the caller still needs the original order. With many equal values a plain partition keeps one side huge, so the worst case is O(n^2).

container/heap needs five methods: Len, Less, Swap, Push and Pop. Push and Pop touch the last item only, so call heap.Push(h, x) and heap.Pop(h). Pop returns any, so write heap.Pop(h).(int) when you use the value.
sort.Ints(nums) sorts in place and changes the caller's slice. Copy with append([]int(nil), nums...) first, as the quickselect version does.

recap.pattern: Heap: kth largest with a min-heap
recap.key: Hold the k biggest in a min-heap. Push each number, pop when over k. The top is the kth largest.
recap.complexity: Heap: O(n log k) time, O(k) space. Quickselect: O(n) average.
moves: Push each number into a min-heap
If size is over k, pop the smallest
Alternative: quickselect toward index n - k
